This file is the evidence that the Python port is faithful; it is not regenerated from Python, ever. Regenerating it from the code it is supposed to check would turn it into a snapshot of whatever the code does today, which is the opposite of what it is for.

_comment_init: roadmap-init captured the same way, before its jq was deleted. Temp paths normalized to /TMP and createdAt frozen -- the only two non-deterministic fields. The dependson-nao-array case records jq EXITING 5 with a raw engine error: the 'dependsOn must be an array' message the code writes was unreachable, because the jq collected it in the same array as the per-entry check and iterating a string aborts. That one case is deliberately NOT reproduced -- there is no faithful port of a crash.

_comment_amend: roadmap-amend-phase captured the same way, before its jq was deleted: 41 payloads covering partial merge by key presence, every unamendable key with its named redirect, every type error, the orphan refusal with its suggestion line in BOTH forms (one added identity fills it in, two leave a placeholder), both unusable-pair reasons, a successful retarget with the downstream rewrite, the cross-phase duplicate block, and the handoff advisory. 205 of 205 field comparisons identical after the port. The 'unchanged' field records that all 32 refusals left roadmap.json byte-for-byte alone.
